name: ruflo
description: The original agent meta-harness. Deploy intelligent multi-player swarms, coordinate autonomous workflows, and build conversational AI systems. Features adaptive memory, self-learning intelligence, RAG integration, and native Claude Code / Codex / Hermes and many more Integrated
one_liner: A free add-on that lets your AI coding assistant split a big task into dozens of specialized sub-agents that coordinate with each other and remember what worked, instead of one agent doing everything alone.
buyer: A technical founder running a small dev team who wants to squeeze more parallel throughput out of AI coding tools they're already paying for, and is comfortable with a fairly complex setup.
business_use_cases: A small dev shop uses the swarm coordination to split a large feature build across many sub-agents running in parallel, shipping client work faster.
A solo founder uses the federation feature to run agents across a home machine and a cloud server that securely share context, without a big DevOps budget.
An agency sells 'AI-accelerated development sprints' to clients, using this as the internal orchestration layer that lets a small team look like a much bigger one.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid setup and tuning services for teams who want the swarm/orchestration benefits but find the 314 MCP tools and 26 CLI commands too much to configure alone.
The project's own hosted UI (flo.ruv.io) hints at the model: sell a simplified, hosted dashboard for non-technical managers to monitor agent swarms.

steal_this: Record a 20-minute 'zero to working swarm' walkthrough video for one common use case (e.g. parallel bug-fixing across a monorepo) and sell it as a $15 course to developers overwhelmed by the tool's surface area.
